subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [3:651] Limitation—no coverage where no individual liability: There can be no D&O coverage for acts for which the directors and officers cannot be held liable individually. For example, only the corporate employer is liable for age and sex discrimination under the ADEA and Title VII; corporate officers and directors have no personal liability. [See Miller v. Maxwell's Int'l, Inc. (9th Cir. 1993) 991 F2d 583, 587 (applying Calif. law)] d. [3:652] Certain liabilities not insurable: D&O policies typically indemnify for “loss” incurred by the directors or officers individually or indemnified by the insured organization. “Loss” is generally defined to exclude certain liabilities incurred by the directors and officers, including: — punitive or exemplary damages; — criminal or civil fines or penalties imposed by law; and — treble damages and other amounts deemed uninsurable by law. 2 e. [3:653] Often no coverage for corporation: Historically, D&O policies covered only the directors and officers of a corporation individually for their wrongful acts; i.e., there was no entity coverage.
